question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize request (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo public-agents-researcher 1.0), Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.challenge: none: the 401 carries no www-authenticate header
decoded.protected-resource-metadata: 200 at https://mcp.datadoghq.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp (the RFC 9728 path for the resource; nothing named it); resource https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp; authorization_servers: https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp (the resource names itself); bearer_methods_supported: header; no scopes_supported
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200 at https://mcp.datadoghq.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/v1/mcp; issuer https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp; authorization, token and registration endpoints all on app.datadoghq.com (oauth2/v1/authorize, api/v2/oauth2/token, api/v2/oauth2/register); oauth_version 2.1; pkce_required true, S256; scopes_supported mcp_all (one scope); grants authorization_code, refresh_token, jwt-bearer with the id-jag grant profile; token auth none only
decoded.rest: GET https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/validate with no Authorization header answers 403 (HTTP/1.1, not 401) with {"errors":["Forbidden"]} and no www-authenticate

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp (the US1 endpoint the vendor documents) answers 401 with a one-word JSON error and no www-authenticate header at all, so nothing in the response tells a client where to authenticate; the RFC 9728 default path answers anyway. That document names the resource as its own authorization server, and the server document then points every endpoint at app.datadoghq.com: authorize, token and dynamic registration. It declares oauth_version 2.1, requires PKCE, lists one scope (mcp_all), accepts public clients only (none is the sole token-auth method), and supports the jwt-bearer grant with the id-jag profile. A keyless GET on the REST API's key-validation endpoint answers 403, not 401, with no challenge. Same 401 as the 2026-09-12 measurement in the entry's notes; the missing challenge header and the single all-or-nothing scope are recorded here for the first time. Nothing here measures what either server does with a credential.
